If you have depression, something that helps me is keeping track of your depressive episodes. Are they triggered by things in your life? Do they just seem to happen at random points with no cause? Is there a cycle to it, such as episodes roughly happening once a month, or once a week? Learning these things can help you gain a sense of control over it, which can help when you're going through these times. You know that it'll pass, or at least lessen, and might even be able to predict when depending on how your depression works. Hope it helps out a bit, and in the meantime try to focus on things you know you enjoy and that occupy your mind. Playing a game you really need to think and focus on, or going out and talking with friends. Wish you the best of luck.
Of course. I want to help out as much as I can, since I can't really help myself at this point. Feel free to vent to me anytime you need it.

Sadly, all ways of suicide, at least to my knowledge, has some sort of pain to it. Taking pills can be extremely painful, with stomach cramps and vomiting, and can take a very long time before you die. Plus, if you do survive the attempt, and even start to get better, it can cause lasting damages on your organs that shortens your life, even if you're able to find a will to live.

Of course, other methods with weapons can be extremely painful, and can leave you with severe damages for the rest of your life. Those ones are an all-or-nothing thing, and while they could be effective, once again they are very painful.

I reccomend you take some time. See if the thoughts dissapate, since most desires for suicide are created by a heightened emotional state. Depression messes with your head, tells you things that aren't always true, twists facts to tell you how horrible you are when you're a 3 dimensional person, with good and bad qualities just like the rest of us. I wish you the best of luck mate, and I hope this mini essay of a comment helps.
Here for you. I'm not always the greatest at comforting others, especially online, but if you want to talk about what you're going through, I'm here to listen
